clue.text: Gail and Marian could be bits on the side

indicators.note: the two names could be something else if their letters were reworked, so the pair is rearranged

explanation.surface: Two women, Gail and Marian, might be someone's lovers on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges GAIL and MARIAN together. 'bits on the side' suggests lovers, sharpening the surface about two women; it actually means notes scribbled in the margins of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: These are scribbled annotations in the margin of a page, literally things written at the side of the text.

clue.text: Broadcast with erotic entertainment from runway

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to air it
a strip, short for striptease, is erotic entertainment

explanation.surface: A broadcast featuring a striptease comes from the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runway' tempts as a fashion catwalk, matching the erotic surface, but it is a landing strip for aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple landing ground for aircraft is a runway, often a rough one away from a main airport.

clue.text: How about that letter !

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at some letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is a mild exclamation of surprise; the second is the spelt-out name of the seventh letter of the alphabet, G.

clue.text: Well-known position after tough youth's departed

parts.note: the position once someone has departed is that there is none of him left, so this gives the word no
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a tough youth of 1950s Britain in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: A famous spot is left behind once the local hard man has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic charade: 'position after tough youth's departed' describes the situation of there being NO TED around. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths known for drape jackets and brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noted is famous or eminent, widely recognised for their achievements.

clue.text: Nothing interrupts Lisa in wild affair

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Nothing interrupts Lisa in wild affair' (7) plainly gives LIAISON (O inside an anagram of LISA IN), but the held answer is LIASONN, three letters off, beyond what answerTypo accepts.
annotationWithheld.clue: Nothing interrupts Lisa in wild affair

clue.text: Voice approval on one new site with conveniences

parts.note: to say amen is to voice approval or agreement
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: a new version of the word site has its letters reworked

explanation.surface: Someone approves a new building site because it has good facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SITE into TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Useful facilities such as shops, parks or toilets are amenities, the comforts a place offers.

clue.text: Wander in the capital, so to speak

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the capital's name matches the spelling of the answer

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy, and famously the capital city of the ancient world

explanation.surface: A tourist strolls around the capital, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to rove about without a fixed plan.

clue.text: Fair in Berkshire town making a further change

indicators.note: the word for fair goes inside the name of the town

parts.note: Reading is a large town in the English county of Berkshire, west of London
just means fair or equitable

explanation.surface: A town fair in Berkshire is reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: READING is a large town in Berkshire, an English county west of London. 'Fair' looks like a funfair noun but is the adjective JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering or adapting something again is a further change to it.

clue.text: French region of wine, and mostly very good

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: also means and, in addition
ace is slang for excellent or very good

explanation.surface: A French wine region is praised as very good, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ALSO to ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region of north-eastern France famous for its white wines such as Riesling and Gewurztraminer.

clue.text: Drink brewed by teenager

indicators.note: brewing mixes and stews things, so the letters of teenager are stirred up

explanation.surface: A teenager makes a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges TEENAGER; it also fits the drink, which helps hide the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea leaves make a pale drink popular in China and Japan.

clue.text: Front of exam slip shows pass

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or small error

explanation.surface: A slip at the start of the exam still earns a pass mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' reads as an exam result in the surface but is the verb used of time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or go by, as in 'weeks elapsed before he replied'.

clue.text: Strongly built tenor inside lacking in emotion

indicators.note: the tenor's letter sits within the word for strongly built

parts.note: something solid is strongly built and sturdy
T is a standard abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A burly tenor shows no feeling on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts T into SOLID.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is impassive, showing little feeling or excitement.

clue.text: Add alcohol to food portions, leading to tears

parts.note: to lace a drink or dish is to add a dash of spirits to it
rations are fixed portions of food

explanation.surface: Spiking the food allowance with booze ends in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests crying, but it means rips (rhymes with 'bears').
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerations are deep cuts or rips in the flesh.

clue.text: Ignore card in sailing boat

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Ignore card in sailing boat' (8) plainly gives SKIPJACK (SKIP + JACK), but the held answer is OKIPJACK; its first letter crosses 5-down, held as the misspelt LIASONN (really LIAISON, which would supply the S), so the typo fix is refused.

clue.text: They may be revelling in cheapness in price as rice discounted

definitions.text: They may be revelling in cheapness in price as rice discounted

indicators.note: letters revelling are running riot, so the words in cheapness in price are rearranged
taken off, so the letters of as and rice are removed from the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: Misers delight in low prices, especially once rice is marked down.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: rearrange IN CHEAPNESS IN PRICE, with the letters of AS RICE removed ('discounted'); 'revelling' marks the shuffle. The whole clue also describes misers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinchpenny is a miser, someone stingy who relishes saving every coin.

clue.text: King squeezed by partner's playing joker

indicators.note: squeezed between the letters of the other piece, so the king's letter goes inside
playing about with the letters of the word mixes them up

parts.note: the possessive is read as the plural partners, giving its final S
K is the standard abbreviation for king in cards and chess

explanation.surface: A partner at the card table is playing the joker, with the king trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges PARTNERS into PRANSTER, and 'squeezed by' puts K inside. 'joker' looks like a card in this bridge-table scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster is a practical joker, someone who plays tricks.

clue.text: Unconventional principal character slammed on the air

indicators.note: words slammed about are knocked out of order, so on the air is rearranged

explanation.surface: A maverick lead actor is panned in a broadcast review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slammed' looks like harsh criticism on the radio, but it signals an anagram of ON THE AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist who lacks the usual heroic virtues, like many a noir detective, is this kind of lead.

clue.text: Aim in studies could be further entries

indicators.note: the word for aim goes inside the word for studies

parts.note: a student reads a subject, so reads means studies
a mission is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An aim in one's studies could lead to further applications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studies' is a verb here: at a British university you 'read' a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitting people again, as to hospital or college, means letting them enter once more.

clue.text: Like one sort of song in geronimo, no diction

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A war cry like 'Geronimo' has no proper diction, so it is no tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across geroniMO NO DICtion.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is a song for one voice, often an ode or lament, so this adjective describes such solo song.

clue.text: Second run in one ground — never again!

indicators.note: the time and run letters sit inside the rearranged word
ground up, the word one is broken and reformed

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run on the scoresheet

explanation.surface: Losing a second run at the same ground makes a cricketer vow never again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges ONE into NOE, and 'in' puts MOR inside it. 'ground' looks like a cricket field but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A declaration that something will not happen again, as in 'that's it, I'm done'.

clue.text: Enter to tackle awkward task and hide

indicators.note: tackling something means taking hold of it, so the word for enter wraps the other letters

parts.note: to go in is to enter

indicators.note: an awkward arrangement of the word task jumbles its letters

explanation.surface: Someone goes in to take on a difficult job and then hides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' scrambles the task to ATSK, which 'to tackle' places within the phrase for enter. 'hide' looks like a verb meaning conceal but is an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Goat leather is an animal's skin, and a skin or pelt is called a hide.

clue.text: Getting home after lodgings, start to eat heartily

indicators.note: the word for home is placed after the word for lodgings

parts.note: digs is British slang for rented lodgings
in means at home

explanation.surface: Arriving home after leaving one's rented room, someone tucks into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: DIGS is everyday British slang for rented rooms, often a student's.
explanation.definitionFit: To tuck in with gusto is the idiom for beginning a meal hungrily.

clue.text: Leave the military in protest on start of bombing

parts.note: a demo, short for demonstration, is a protest march

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A soldier quits the army in protest at the start of a bombing campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMOB is British shorthand for demobilise, release from the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discharged from the armed forces after service is called being demobilised.

clue.text: Officer on the beat in failure to take responsibility

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
a policeman on the beat is out patrolling the streets

explanation.surface: A patrolling policeman is accused of dodging his duty.
explanation.definitionFit: An evasion or dodge of a duty is the informal noun for avoiding commitment.

clue.text: Greek courtier from Delos caught out drinking in the morning

indicators.note: one piece drinks the other in, taking it inside
letters put out are knocked out of place and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the name of a Greek island
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A Greek courtier from the island of Delos was caught drunk before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' mixes the island and the caught letter into DOCLES, and 'drinking' takes the morning abbreviation inside. Damocles sat feasting under a sword hung by a single hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtier of Dionysius of Syracuse who sat beneath a sword hung by a single hair is the classical figure meant.

clue.text: Trim and endearingly pretty, almost

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cute means attractive in an endearing way

explanation.surface: A neat, nearly adorable haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CUTE to CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim hair or a hedge is to cut it back a little.

clue.text: Cries from cat heard in group of stables

explanation.surface: A cat's mewing can be heard around the stables.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense means the thin miaowing calls a cat makes; the second means a row of stables round a yard, many now converted into houses.

clue.text: Music associated with Shakespearian character at lowest level

parts.note: rock is a genre of popular music
Nick Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream who is given an ass's head

explanation.surface: A rock gig staged with a Shakespeare character hits a new low.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTOM is the weaver given an ass's head in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the lowest possible point, as when prices or spirits can fall no further.
